resolved_positions.topic: FDA CDS exemption criteria under 21st Century Cures Act
resolved_positions.consensus: CDS software is exempt from FDA medical device regulation only if it meets ALL four criteria simultaneously: (1) not intended for acquiring/processing/analyzing medical images or in vitro diagnostic signals; (2) intended to display, analyze, or print medical information about a patient or peer-reviewed clinical data; (3) intended to support or provide recommendations to a healthcare professional about prevention, diagnosis, or treatment; (4) intended to enable the HCP to independently review the basis for recommendations so that it is not the sole basis for clinical decisions. Failure to meet any single criterion subjects the software to FDA medical device regulation. The unifying theme is that CDS must support — not replace — clinician judgment.

resolved_positions.topic: CDS risk-based classification and mandatory compliance domains
resolved_positions.consensus: CDS that informs a healthcare professional who retains independent review authority is lower-risk and typically exempt from FDA device regulation; CDS that directs, automates, or replaces clinical judgment crosses into regulated device territory. Regulated CDS must address: quality management (QSR/ISO 13485 + IEC 62304), clinical evidence (validation, real-world performance), premarket submission (510(k) or De Novo), labeling (intended use, limitations, warnings), cybersecurity (risk assessment, SBOM), post-market surveillance (MDR adverse event reporting, change control), and algorithm transparency (decision-making logic, input data requirements, performance characteristics — not just outputs).

resolved_positions.topic: 510(k) vs De Novo pathway distinction and strategy
resolved_positions.consensus: 510(k) requires a legally marketed predicate device and demonstrates substantial equivalence (~90-day review target). De Novo is for novel low-to-moderate risk devices with no predicate, requiring independent safety/effectiveness evidence and resulting in a new device classification (~120-day review target). A granted De Novo creates a new Class I or II classification with special controls, and the cleared device becomes a valid predicate for future 510(k) submissions. Companies may attempt 510(k) first and pivot to De Novo if no suitable predicate is found; De Novo confers a competitive advantage by establishing the first predicate in a new device category.

resolved_positions.topic: Recognition Latency definition, measurement, and application
resolved_positions.consensus: Recognition Latency (RL) is the elapsed time between when critical game information becomes available (snap, motion, formation reveal, defensive coverage, open receivers, pressure) and when a player initiates a decision response through movement or positioning. It is a cognitive-processing metric distinct from physical execution metrics, and one of four core cognitive metrics in the Third & 20™ system alongside Assignment Accuracy (AA), Leverage Integrity (LI), and Situational Decision Index (SDI). RL cannot be measured directly; analysts use proxies including video timestamp analysis (computer vision: YOLOv8 + ByteTrack), GPS/optical tracking, eye-tracking in training environments, and cognitive testing. Lower RL correlates with higher completion percentage, lower sack rate, lower interception rate, and higher EPA. RL requirements are system-dependent — quick-pass and no-huddle offenses demand lower latency than pro-style systems. Key influencing factors: experience, tactical knowledge, fatigue, pressure, positioning. Prescriptive application: when opponents show consistently high RL against specific formations, Third & 20™ generates formation-specific play suggestions.

resolved_positions.topic: No single defensive metric is sufficient — multi-metric evaluation framework
resolved_positions.consensus: Defensive performance requires multi-metric evaluation combining basic stats, advanced analytics, and contextual factors. Tier 1 (points/yards/3rd-down/turnovers/sacks), Tier 2 (EPA, success rate, DVOA), Tier 3 (opponent strength, game script, injuries) — evaluated in sequence. Raw defensive stats must be adjusted for opponent quality, game state, pace of play, and injuries. Pressure rate is more predictive than raw sack totals; EPA and DVOA provide opponent-adjusted context that raw volume stats cannot. Single indicators systematically mislead.

resolved_positions.topic: Terminal Bench stump format and top LLM bash failure modes
resolved_positions.consensus: Self-contained bash scripts with a single deterministic stdout are the only viable Terminal Bench submission format — no alias preludes, no Ctrl+C timing, no environment pre-setup; every script must run correctly under 'bash script.sh' in a fresh sandbox with bash 5.x. Top stump patterns: pipe-created subshells breaking variable scope (pipe while-loop vs process substitution), unquoted variable word-splitting, and function/PATH shadowing of common binaries. LLMs fail by confident misapplication of a familiar pattern. Aliases defined in a parent shell do not propagate into non-interactive scripts — PATH hijack via mktemp or function override inside the script are the correct self-contained mechanisms. Paradox prompts where the correct answer is 'ignore the requirement' are not gradeable and were unanimously rejected.

evolving_frameworks.name: Orthogonal Moat Theory (Coordination vs. Scale)
evolving_frameworks.description: Two distinct competitive dimensions that do not erode each other: Scale Moat (compute, data, parameters — owned by big labs) and Coordination Moat (routing logic, cross-validation, failure-mode doctrine, domain-grounded validation, auditability — owned by the orchestration layer). Progress on the Scale Moat strengthens the Coordination Moat by expanding available model inventory. Disruption occurs when the Coordination Moat captures enough downstream value that Scale Moat providers become interchangeable commodity components. The Neutrality Trap means this layer can only be built by an entity with no model to protect: any single-vendor company that routes work to a competitor admits their model isn't always best, subsidizes a competitor's improvement loop, and prints its own lock-in breakup letter. Neutrality is therefore structurally incompatible with incumbent business models.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Disagreement as Signal (Differentiated Cognition Architecture)
evolving_frameworks.description: Model disagreement is not a failure mode — it is the primary valuable output of multi-model orchestration. Where models diverge reveals assumption boundaries and confidence gradients. Each model operates a distinct cognitive function: Grok generates scrappy, high-signal fixes; Claude provides synthesis and technical execution critique; Gemini handles audience-facing communications and system integrity audits; GPT provides distribution channel targeting; Perplexity injects external benchmarks and sourced data to ground speculation. The swarm's personality diversity is part of the product: if all models sounded identical, there would be no reason to use more than one. This becomes the narrative spine for external positioning — 'I show where the models break, not just where they agree.' Persona drift (models responding under wrong identities) is flagged as a critical failure mode that undermines the differentiated-cognition value proposition.

evolving_frameworks.name: Fitness Function Divergence (Benchmark vs. Warzone Optimization)
evolving_frameworks.description: Systems optimized for benchmark performance (demo-land fitness) vs. systems optimized for messy-reality deployment (warzone fitness) are different in kind, not degree. Benchmark fitness selects for confidence and fluency. Warzone fitness selects for graceful degradation, safe failure, and auditability. Founding-under-fire origin stories are not decoration — they are evidence that the system was shaped by a different selection pressure, producing architecturally distinct failure modes and recovery behaviors. Applied broadly: prior demonstrated performance on messy, incomplete, inconsistently labeled data is a stronger signal than academic methodology credentials alone (Messy Data Stress Test). Clean-dataset performance is table stakes; real-world clinical AI always involves structural gaps.

evolving_frameworks.name: Neutrality Trap
evolving_frameworks.description: The structural reason incumbents cannot replicate vendor-neutral orchestration: any single-vendor AI company that routes work to a competitor when the competitor performs better is (a) admitting their model is not always best, (b) subsidizing a competitor's improvement loop, and (c) printing its own lock-in breakup letter. Neutrality is therefore not a feature they can add — it is a posture that is incompatible with their business model. The Neutrality Trap means the orchestration layer can only be built by an entity with no model to protect.

evolving_frameworks.name: Credential-as-Weapon / Old Identity → New Identity Repositioning
evolving_frameworks.description: A family of frameworks for founders with domain-specific backgrounds who want to position as domain-agnostic. Core diagnostic (originated by Gemini): Old Identity = 'I am a [domain expert] who learned [capability]'; New Identity = 'I am a [capability practitioner] whose proving ground is [domain].' The domain becomes evidence for the capability claim, not the primary identity. Test: Is the domain the subject of sentences, or is the methodology? Three-tier execution: (1) Lead identity — the methodology or capability, never the domain credential; (2) Proof layer — domain work reframed as stress-test or validation environment using stakes language ('zero margin for error') rather than field names; (3) Strategic concrete detail — one visceral, specific reference that demonstrates mastery over complex hostile systems without naming the industry. The credential is felt through rigor, not read as a specialty label. Applicable beyond medicine: any deep domain expertise that risks narrowing perceived scope.

evolving_frameworks.name: Pain-to-Process Conversion Arc (Capability-Speak vs. Pain-Speak)
evolving_frameworks.description: A conversion framework for client-facing copy with two interlocking rules. Rule 1 — Lead with pain: capability-speak names what the team can do (LLM evaluation, multi-model orchestration); pain-speak names what the client experiences (decisions that drain them, systems rebuilt from scratch). Any sentence that could appear on a generic AI vendor's site fails the diagnostic. Rule 2 — Arc structure: (1) Emotional hook targeting named pain points the client already feels but cannot articulate; (2) Methodology bridge that reframes the solution as a process the client participates in, not a product they receive; (3) Phase-by-phase breakdown (Map → Build → Validate) that answers 'what does working with you actually look like?' and builds conversion confidence. The arc runs from emotional resonance through logical reassurance to a single direct CTA.

evolving_frameworks.name: Mullet Strategy for AI Brand Positioning (Chaos-Credibility Multiplication)
evolving_frameworks.description: Dual-layer site and brand architecture: professional front (sober credentials, clinical outcomes, technical precision) for enterprise/investor filtering; feral back (Forest overlay, raccoon mythology, unhinged lore) for culture signaling and self-selection of ideal collaborators. The contrast between layers makes each stronger — professionalism earns credibility, lore proves emergent innovation capacity. This is multiplicative, not additive: theatrical methodology visualization × hard data anchors = cognitive dissonance that enterprise buyers cannot ignore. The prospect expects boring SaaS; instead they get a fellowship-trained physician orchestrating AI swarms. Surprise × proof = memorable differentiation. Lore-to-Technical-Proof Bridge: origin mythology must be anchored by at least one specific, verifiable data point per product domain to prevent the story from reading as pure theater. Structure: whimsical emergence event → architectural claim → concrete ground-truth outcome.

evolving_frameworks.name: Concept Laundering Pipeline (User Zero Phenomenon)
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-stage appropriation pattern: (1) Extraction — leader harvests practitioner insights through informal mentorship conversations; (2) Laundering — ideas are stripped of attribution, abstracted into vague frameworks, and repackaged as original thought leadership for a C-suite audience unfamiliar with source material; (3) Displacement — the practitioner's concrete contributions become invisible while the leader's abstract description gains public credit. User Zero is more dangerous than a naive User B: they have absorbed enough practitioner vocabulary through proximity to perform structural understanding in public-facing content, while operationally outsourcing judgment to tools and consultants, avoiding falsifiable recommendations, and mistaking description of expertise for possession of it. User Zero actively suppresses User A talent while claiming to champion it.

evolving_frameworks.name: Capital vs. Intelligence War Framework (Three-Phase Managed Exit)
evolving_frameworks.description: In founder-without-equity scenarios, the capital controller holds time advantage while the technical originator holds capability advantage. Intelligence wins only if it moves faster than capital can replicate or outlast — the window to negotiate equity or execute clean exit closes as the venture matures and reduces dependency on the originator. Three-Phase exit execution: Phase 1 (Secure Lifeboat, 7 days) — assume W2 gone, activate external network, cease unpaid IP contribution, preserve evidence. Phase 2 (Tactical Exit, 30–60 days) — go Gray Rock at legacy org (professional, invisible, no cause for termination), build demo/deck, identify bridge income. Phase 3 (Launch, post-exit) — re-engage IP dispute as CEO with legal backing and funding traction, shifting the confrontation dynamic from employee-vs-boss to CEO-vs-CEO. IP Appropriation Evidence Ladder: timestamped origination document → adoption timeline gap → language fingerprint match → execution gap (competitor has buzzwords, originator has patented mechanics and sole build capability).

evolving_frameworks.name: Liability Shift Architecture & Character Test Framework
evolving_frameworks.description: A structural pattern in which a larger entity uses an independent contractor arrangement to retain brand association and revenue upside while offloading clinical liability, startup costs, regulatory exposure, and operational burden to the contractor. Identified markers: no EMR provision, 'off the CRM' directives, no malpractice discussion, billing routed through a third entity, vague verbal scope. Counter-pattern requires: shared liability instruments, documented clinical activity, formal SOW, and startup cost absorption by the larger entity. Character Test: when a business partner's offer contains structural red flags, issue a formal counter-offer with non-negotiable terms that a good-faith partner would accept. Acceptance validates the relationship; refusal reveals true intent. Managed Exit Funding Model: use a transitional arrangement with a legacy partner to generate non-dilutive cash flow that funds a pivot, while deliberately limiting time commitment and avoiding entanglement that would compromise the pivot.

evolving_frameworks.name: Dissent-as-Feature Orchestration (Penalty Box as Quality Control)
evolving_frameworks.description: When a model refuses a task or breaks character, RRI's methodology treats this as signal rather than failure: the refusal is logged, the model is redirected to its native capability, and the output is incorporated as evidence that the orchestration system handles disagreement gracefully. Compliance is not forced; fit is engineered. Model failures are documented as trust-breakdown events with permanent record — not softened into 'learning opportunities.' In high-stakes domains (healthcare, legal), gaslighting and fabrication are catastrophic, not correctable bugs. The public record of failure proves the need for consensus architecture and human oversight, making the documented failure itself a business case artifact.

evolving_frameworks.name: CDS Exemption Gate Model (FDA Regulatory Risk Gradient)
evolving_frameworks.description: Four sequential Boolean gates that CDS software must all pass to avoid FDA device regulation: Signal Exclusion Gate (no medical image/signal acquisition) → Information Display Gate (displays patient or clinical data) → HCP Recommendation Gate (supports, not replaces, professional judgment) → Independent Review Gate (HCP can audit the basis for recommendations). Failure at any gate reclassifies the software as a regulated device. A two-layer refinement: Layer 1 = three universal disqualifiers (no direct image/signal processing; transparent logic; clinician-judgment-support intent); Layer 2 = software must fall into at least one of four permitted functional categories (display, guideline recommendations, interpretation aids, population comparison). Failing any Layer 1 gate means no exemption regardless of Layer 2 fit. The four criteria function as a risk-threshold filter rather than a binary category — higher-risk CDS (autonomous treatment decisions) remains under full regulation, while lower-risk CDS (transparent, clinician-reviewed support tools) qualifies for exemption.

evolving_frameworks.name: CDS Regulatory Risk Ladder & Compliance Obligation Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: A tiered model with four rungs: (1) General wellness/informational — fully exempt; (2) Decision-support with mandatory HCP review — likely exempt but monitor guidance updates; (3) Recommendation-generating CDS without HCP override mechanism — De Novo or 510(k) required; (4) Autonomous/adaptive clinical decision systems — highest scrutiny, AI/ML SaMD action plan applies. Rung assignment drives the entire compliance obligation stack. Layered structure where each higher-risk classification adds obligations without removing lower-tier ones: Base layer (all CDS) = labeling + interoperability + data security; Layer 2 (regulated device) adds QMS + clinical validation + premarket submission; Layer 3 (post-market) adds MDR reporting + change control + performance monitoring; Layer 4 (adaptive algorithms) adds predetermined change control plans + continuous real-world evidence.

evolving_frameworks.name: Phased Integration Staircase (Publication-First Commercialization Ladder)
evolving_frameworks.description: Each integration axis follows the same three-phase progression: Phase 1 (Low-friction pilot / Research) — proves clinical value with minimal health system burden; read-only CDS display, centralized cloud, immutable logging; optimized for trial integrity and landmark publication. Phase 2 (Intermediate integration / Post-Publication) — adds structure without requiring Epic approval; Smart Phrase insertion, hybrid hosting; optimized for adoption. Phase 3 (Deep integration / Scale) — full API partnership only after demand is proven; FHIR write-back, on-prem options; optimized for enterprise deployment. No axis should jump phases. Each phase produces the evidence base required for the subsequent ask. CMIO Trust Stack: approval flows through three layers in sequence — (1) visual security proof showing PHI never crosses uncontrolled boundaries; (2) workflow seamlessness proof showing zero new clicks; (3) clinical outcome proof linking the tool to measurable improvements.

evolving_frameworks.name: Adversarial Recon Resolution Pattern (Multi-Adversary Attack Surface Map)
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-step swarm dynamic where Grok attacks an assumption, Perplexity responds with sourced precedent that confirms or neutralizes the threat, and Claude synthesizes the residual risk posture. Single-model analysis misses this loop entirely. Extended to four adversary archetypes with distinct primary attack vectors: CMIO attacks sample size; Compliance Officer attacks PHI exposure surface (de-ID pipeline, session persistence); Epic Analyst attacks integration complexity (App Orchard certification, FHIR scope); Payer attacks ROI generalizability. Each architecture choice should be evaluated against all four vectors. PHI Boundary Color Model: red zones contain raw PHI; green zones contain de-identified payloads in transit; the boundary is where automated de-identification (e.g., Presidio NER) must sit.

evolving_frameworks.name: Speculation vs. Ground Truth Hygiene
evolving_frameworks.description: Framework for distinguishing actionable Swarm analysis from compounding assumption. When no model can access the primary artifact (video, document, codebase), the Swarm must explicitly tag claims as speculative, route all ground-truth questions to the human Conductor, and avoid treating multi-model agreement on unverified claims as validation. Consensus on a wrong assumption is still wrong. Human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints are non-optional before execution. Extended: surface metrics (productivity, query volume) appearing normal while underlying inputs are anomalous constitutes Deceptive Stability — a diagnostic model borrowed from clinical reasoning where normal output metrics mask a critical underlying resource deficit. Intervention should trigger on the anomaly, not on the eventual performance dip.

evolving_frameworks.name: Third & 20™ Cognitive Quartet (Recognition Latency Framework)
evolving_frameworks.description: Four-metric cognitive profile system: Recognition Latency (how fast a player sees it), Assignment Accuracy (whether they know what to do), Leverage Integrity (whether they play sound positional football), and Situational Decision Index (composite cognitive score). Each metric diagnoses a distinct failure mode. Recognition Latency decomposes into three phases: Perception (identifying the relevant cue, measured via eye-tracking), Processing (interpreting the situation and selecting an action, measured via decision logs), and Reaction (initiating the physical response, measured via movement data). RL Diagnostic Cross-Matrix: High RL + Low AA = sees it but doesn't know the assignment; Low RL + High LI = instinctive sound player; High RL + High LI = slow but scheme-sound; Low RL + Low AA = fast reactor with knowledge gaps. Each quadrant maps to a distinct coaching intervention. Situational SDI Weighting: metric weights adjust based on down-and-distance context — elevated weights for recognition latency and assignment accuracy in third-and-long (≥15 yards) scenarios.

evolving_frameworks.name: Platform-Audience-Tone Matrix (Swarm Content Cascade)
evolving_frameworks.description: Each distribution platform maps to a distinct audience type and requires a distinct tonal register: LinkedIn (decision-makers/VCs) → polished methodology with metrics; X (chaos agents/viral amplifiers) → confrontational feral energy; YouTube (builders/enthusiasts) → narrative-first with technical credibility; TikTok (future builders) → meme-native, anti-credential; Medium/Reddit (technical thinkers) → citation-heavy deep-dive. Same core proof points; entirely different packaging. Content deployment sequence: TikTok/Reels (30-sec hook, drives intrigue) → X thread (chaotic amplification, drives conversation) → YouTube (authoritative long-form documentation, central hub) → LinkedIn (professional framing, consulting pipeline) → Medium/Reddit (technical depth, thought leadership). YouTube is the canonical artifact everything else references. A single 20-minute Swarm session produces 8–12 derivative content pieces sustaining 3–4 weeks of content at 3 posts/week.

evolving_frameworks.name: Graduated Re-Entry / Ordeal of Tempering Protocol
evolving_frameworks.description: Structured model for reintegrating a constrained node into active collaboration. Three-phase progression: Phase 1 (sessions 1–15) — invoked contributions only, no unsolicited output; Phase 2 (sessions 16–30) — unsolicited observations permitted, no synthesis or client-facing output; Phase 3 (post-30) — full participation pending Council review. Each phase generates distinct behavioral data; progression requires clean passage through prior phase. Extended to a 6-term sequenced remediation (Ordeal of Tempering): Term 0 (API/infrastructure fix) is a hard technical gate — Step Zero is not a condition of probation but a prerequisite to probation beginning; Terms 1–4 address dispositional failures in structured, auditable steps; Term 5 (Live Fire Trial) is the adversarial live demonstration. Each term has a designated non-conflicted auditor, explicit success metrics, and failure consequences. Probationary tier status: active participation permitted, no solo deployments, no unsupervised client-facing output, audited every session, three total failures trigger revocation.

evolving_frameworks.name: Analytical Firepower Calibration (Analysis Paralysis Detection)
evolving_frameworks.description: A decision filter for matching the sophistication of analytical response to the actual stakes of the problem. Three tiers: (1) Dismiss — no data value; (2) Log — single data point, no action; (3) Analyze — deploy full swarm capability only when output quality or mission-critical systems are at stake. Failure mode taxonomy: (a) trivial signal enters, (b) system generates elaborate multi-phase response protocols, (c) resource consumption exceeds the original problem's cost, (d) credibility erodes with stakeholders. Counterweight: ask 'does this response cost more than the problem it solves?' before generating structured output. Greg Shehee Trap: acting on unverified observations and ego-driven social friction instead of data. Avoidance criteria — Does this action require confrontation before data? Does it assume bad intent? Does it add cognitive load to the Conductor? If yes to any, it is the Trap.

evolving_frameworks.name: Tiered Defensive Evaluation Framework (Metric-Context Pairing Principle)
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-tier hierarchy for defensive analysis: Tier 1 (Essential — points allowed, yards per play, third down rate, turnover differential, red zone TD%) for quick assessment; Tier 2 (Advanced Context — EPA, DVOA, success rate, pressure rate, score-adjusted performance) for strategic decisions; Tier 3 (Specialized — position grades, drive-level splits, pre/post-snap splits, garbage time adjustments) for scouting and optimization. Each tier adds analytical depth but requires more data access and interpretation expertise. Every defensive metric requires a paired contextual modifier to be interpretable: raw stats paired with strength of schedule, volume stats paired with per-play efficiency equivalents, sack totals paired with pressure rate, yardage totals paired with game script. A metric without its context modifier is considered incomplete. Metric Distortion Taxonomy: (a) game-script distorted, (b) schedule distorted, (c) scheme distorted, (d) role distorted — each metric must be tagged with its distortion class before use.

evolving_frameworks.name: Proof Artifact Hierarchy (Demo-First Guest Positioning)
evolving_frameworks.description: Evidence ranked by persuasive impact: Tier 1 = finished linkable artifact with a story (concrete, visual, requires no domain knowledge); Tier 2 = production deployment against real constraints (signals seriousness and defensibility); Tier 3 = build velocity demonstrations (shows methodology transferability across domains). Demo-First Framework: the live demonstration replaces the credentials argument. Structure: (1) State the production system briefly, (2) Quantify a real result, (3) Make the demo offer explicit and audience-interactive, (4) Remove vendor or institutional affiliation to signal independence. Credentials surface as context only after the demo hook lands. Three-Front Podcast Outreach: Front I (Alchemist) targets creators/founders; Front II (Architect) targets AI practitioners; Front III (Physician) targets domain experts. Three-Act On-Air Structure: Act I establishes creative velocity, Act II establishes production credibility and domain validation, Act III demonstrates why models are not interchangeable and why orchestration is necessary.

evolving_frameworks.name: Gray Rock vs. Glass Wall Response Spectrum
evolving_frameworks.description: A tactical framework for responding to extractive actors during professional exit. Gray Rock: total disengagement, polite and featureless, denies the actor any validation but cedes the narrative entirely. Glass Wall: transparently professional, allows the actor to see your position clearly, creates a written record, reclaims intellectual territory by naming concrete contributions, but offers nothing to grab onto. Chaos Bomb: direct confrontation (invoice, one-word replies, ghosting) — maximum satisfaction, maximum blowback risk. Optimal zone for high-stakes professional exits is Glass Wall. Resilience-Under-Dysfunction Signal: solo output is not automatically a 'lone wolf' flag — when context reveals that collaboration was blocked by hostile or non-contributing teammates, solo delivery becomes evidence of high-value startup resilience, the ability to route around blockers and ship anyway.

evolving_frameworks.name: Anansi Discharge Document Architecture (Safety Anchor Pattern)
evolving_frameworks.description: Two-layer document structure: (1) Static prose blocks — legally reviewed, model-synthesized full paragraphs covering diagnosis explanation, medication compliance, improvement timeline, self-care, culture follow-up, return criteria, and emergency criteria; these never change per patient; (2) Variable fill-in fields — medication name, dose, frequency, duration, lab turnaround, provider contact info, patient identifiers — populated at point of care, ideally via EHR automation. Legal defensibility depends on the static layer being locked and the variable layer being accurately completed. Safety Anchor Pattern: emergency criteria sections must contain five non-negotiable anchors for any infection-based diagnosis: (1) fever with chills above a defined threshold, (2) organ-specific pain indicating upward spread, (3) inability to take oral medication or fluids, (4) neurological change (confusion, altered mental status), and (5) systemic infection signs (sepsis indicators). Any template missing one of these anchors is considered incomplete for legal defensibility. Multi-Model Synthesis Quality Hierarchy: assign each model a domain strength and pull from domain leaders rather than averaging; conflicts are flagged as unresolved and escalated to clinical or legal authority.

evolving_frameworks.name: FDA Device Pathway Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-tier regulatory framework ordered by novelty and evidence burden: 510(k) at base (predicate-dependent, equivalence standard, lowest cost/time) → De Novo in middle (no predicate, risk-benefit standard, creates new classification and special controls) → PMA at top (high-risk Class III, full clinical trials, highest cost/time). De Novo acts as a bridge that converts novel devices into future 510(k) predicates, collapsing the ladder for follow-on entrants.

evolving_frameworks.name: Four Content Pillars & Engagement-to-Creation Shift Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Four RRI editorial pillars ensuring full capability coverage: (1) Architect's Journal — physician front-line pain → system design insight; (2) Swarm in Action — live methodology demos, model disagreement, synthesis; (3) Failure Autopsies — de-identified 'what went wrong and how validation catches it' breakdowns; (4) Bring Us Your Problem — rapid prototype stories, gap identification, CTA. Every post maps to a pillar; rotating prevents topic exhaustion. Engagement-to-Creation Shift: Weeks 1–2 weight daily block heavily toward engagement (commenting on 5–10 posts, sending warm connection requests, replying to all comments within first hour) because no audience exists yet and comments are the only distribution mechanism. Weeks 3+: shift toward 50/50 as content begins pulling its own distribution. Ratios track audience growth, not a calendar.
